title: Cancer Free Since 2016 – Featured Healing Story
content: Cancer Free Since 2016 – Featured Healing StoryRadical Remission ProjectApr 18, 20182 min readUpdated: Nov 9, 2023Ella began to feel ill and lost weight in 2013. She thought it was an ulcer due to huge amounts of stress. She went for an ultrasound and found a lump the size of a tennis ball on her colon. It was cut out and tested positive for colon cancer stage 1. She refused chemo and made changes to her diet and lifestyle. This is her story in her own words:I lost weight and felt ill in 2013. I thought it was an ulcer due to the huge amount of stress I was under. I went for a ultrasound and found a lump the size of a tennis ball on my colon. Had it cut out and it tested positive for colon cancer stage 1. I was clear and did not do chemo or any treatment other than a slight change to lifestyle and diet. My follow up scan in September 2016 found a 5 cm lesion on the liver. I had that surgically removed plus two more growths on the colon. PET scan all clear after surgery – refused chemo again. I made radical changes to my lifestyle and diet, plus I added a whole lot of natural therapies. I’ve had two scans so far and am all clear.Both times I lost weight and had problems with my stomach (pain, foul smelling stools, feeling of fullness after a little bit of food). Blood tests did not show cancer – only diagnosed by labs after surgery. I did not try conventional treatment (chemo) because it only gave me a success rate of 5% the first time around and 15-30% the second time round. Those were not good enough odds for me when I weighed them against the side effects of the chemo.I mistakenly believed the doctors in 2013 when they told me “it’s cut out, so there’s no need to worry.” No one mentioned circulating stem cells. After the first diagnosis, I decided to make some changes to my diet and lifestyle. Getting divorced was one of the changes I made – an extremely abusive marriage was not helping my healing, so I opted out. I realize now that the changes I made were not radical enough to support continued healing. My stress levels never really went down much and the second tumor was discovered in September 2016 a few months after a particularly stressful event related to the father of my children.I also had genetic testing done which showed that my body does not have the ability to produce glutathione, which is a main enzyme used for Phase I liver detoxification. To compensate for that, I take IV glutathione weekly and juice kale and other greens daily. I have done a whole lot more work on the spiritual side as well. I currently feeling healthier and happier than I have ever felt.Did you know that The Radical Remission Project puts out a monthly newsletter with even more stories of healing as well as upcoming events and the latest news?! validation.statistical_improbability_notes: Stage 1 colon cancer treated with surgery is not rare to clear; later liver lesion and additional colon growths were also surgically removed with PET all clear. Narrative frames refusal of chemo and use of lifestyle/natural therapies as key, but surgery is a major conventional treatment.
validation.extraction_notes: Many 'natural therapies' and 'spiritual work' are not specified; unclear whether liver lesion was confirmed metastatic colon cancer vs. separate lesion, but treated in the cancer narrative context.

analysis.case_summary: Ella was diagnosed with stage 1 colon cancer in 2013 after an ultrasound found a tennis-ball-sized colon lump; it was surgically removed and tested positive. A follow-up scan in Sept 2016 found a 5 cm liver lesion and two more colon growths, which were surgically removed; PET scan was all clear and she reports subsequent scans remain clear while refusing chemotherapy and making major lifestyle, dietary, and spiritual changes.
key_healing_factors: Surgical removal of colon tumor (2013) and later liver lesion plus additional colon growths (2016)
Refusal of chemotherapy and active self-directed decision-making
Radical lifestyle and diet changes (details limited; daily green juicing mentioned)
Weekly IV glutathione following genetic testing indicating impaired glutathione production
Leaving an extremely abusive marriage (divorce) and addressing stress
unique_features: Genetic testing reported inability to produce glutathione; weekly IV glutathione used
Explicit linkage between stress/relationship events and timing of recurrence
Refused chemotherapy twice, citing low perceived success rates (5% then 15–30%)
analysis.analysis_notes: This is not a pure spontaneous remission because surgery was performed; remission is described as post-surgical with imaging (PET) confirmation. Specific alternative therapies besides IV glutathione and green juicing are not detailed.
